request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change and the main tree-numbering test passes, along with scenarios 1 and 2. Scenario 3 still fails, at a check in the test itself that no app can pass.

**The change.** When a claim is opened on a sheet without period numbering, it now gets the number after the highest one given on any sheet of its tree. The tree means the topmost parent plus everything under it.
- `SheetService.tree(id)` lists the sheets of the tree.
- `PeriodService.nextClaimNumber` locks the sheet and the tree's top sheet, finds the highest last-number across the tree and gives the next one. Locking the top sheet means two sheets in the same tree can't hand out the same number at once.
- `Sheet.nextClaimNumberAfter(...)` keeps each sheet's last-number up to date. Numbers given earlier are left as they are.
- Period numbering (`P1-1`, and the `X-n` numbers for claims outside any period) stays per sheet. No schema change was needed.

**A second fix scenario 3 needed.** In that scenario, adding "Ada" with terms 3 and a contact is refused. The people form kept those values, so the next person added, Cam, was saved with them (`PERSON_ADDED … name=Cam grade=A terms=3 contact=ada@x`). That made his claim overdue and broke the expected audit. A refused add now clears the form but still shows the error, in `people.ts`. This bug was already there: scenario 3 failed at the same step when I turned my numbering change off.

**Where scenario 3 still fails.** At `acceptance.spec.ts:1073` (and again at `:1151`) the test expects `sheet-parent` to read the literal text `__SHEET__-p`. The parent was set to `${sheet}-p`, a random id, so the screen shows something like `smvk34k1avumm-p`. It looks like a placeholder that was never filled in when the test was written. I'm not allowed to edit the spec, and making the app show that placeholder would be a fake, so I left it. Since the run stops there, I haven't been able to check the rest of scenario 3 after line 1073. If the spec gets corrected to `${sheet}-p`, the next `bin/e2e` run will check the remainder.
